either for self-review or to understand a teammate's work.

By default, shows checkpoints on the current branch. Pass a checkpoint ID or
commit SHA as a positional argument to explain a specific item, or use flags.

Viewing specific items:
  entire checkpoint explain <id-or-sha>           Auto-detects checkpoint ID or commit SHA
  entire checkpoint explain --checkpoint <id>     Force interpretation as checkpoint ID
  entire checkpoint explain --commit <ref>        Force interpretation as commit ref

Checkpoints in another repo:
  entire checkpoint explain <id-or-sha> --repo gh/owner/name
  entire checkpoint explain <id-or-sha> --repo et/project/repo
                 Explain a checkpoint owned by another repository — the
                 drill-down for a cross-repo 'entire search' hit. Reads it from
                 that repo's Entire API; nothing is written to this repo.
                 Needs a full checkpoint ID (12-char hex or 26-char ULID) or a full commit SHA
                 (positional, --checkpoint, or --commit) and a checkpoint that
                 has been pushed. A commit SHA is resolved to its checkpoint
                 by that repo's Entire API, so prefixes cannot be used here.

Filtering the list view:
  --session      Filter checkpoints by session ID (or prefix)

Output verbosity levels (when explaining a specific item):
  Default:         Detailed view with scoped prompts (ID, session, tokens, intent, prompts, files)
  --short          Summary only (ID, session, timestamp, tokens, intent)
  --full           Parsed full transcript (all prompts/responses from entire session)
  --raw-transcript Raw transcript file (JSONL format)

Machine-readable export modes (additive surface for external consumers):
  --json           Metadata-only JSON. Lists checkpoints when no target is given;
                   emits a single checkpoint envelope when a target is supplied,
                   including its subagent task records under "tasks".
                   Transcript bytes are NEVER embedded in the JSON envelope.
  --transcript     Stream stored checkpoint transcript bytes (JSONL) to stdout
                   for the selected session. Same bytes as --raw-transcript
                   while checkpoints v1 is the checkpoint store.
  --session-index  Pick a session within a multi-session checkpoint (0-based).
                   Defaults to the latest session. Only meaningful with
                   --transcript or --raw-transcript.
  --task           With --transcript, stream a subagent's stored transcript
                   instead, selected by tool_use_id or agent_id (as listed
                   under "tasks" in --json).
  --limit          Cap the number of checkpoints returned by the list view.
                   Defaults to 100. When the cap is hit, a stderr note
                   says how many were skipped. Only meaningful with --json.

Summary generation:
  --generate    Generate an AI summary for the checkpoint. This is the only
                part of this command that writes: it stores the summary on the
                checkpoint and spends tokens with the configured summary
                provider. Every other mode only reads.
  --force       Regenerate even if a summary already exists (requires --generate)

Performance options:
  --search-all  Remove branch/depth limits when searching for commits (may be slow)

Checkpoint detail view shows:
  - Author of the checkpoint
  - Associated git commits that reference the checkpoint
  - Prompts and responses from the session

Note: --session filters the list view; the positional arg, --commit, and --checkpoint are mutually exclusive.

When to use this:
Reading a checkpoint is free: with no flags, or with --json, --full,
--transcript or --raw-transcript, this only reads and is safe to run
whenever you need the context. --generate is the exception — it writes a
summary onto the checkpoint and spends tokens with the summary provider,
so pass it only when the user asked for a summary. To see what subagents
did, read "tasks" in --json, then stream one subagent's transcript with
--transcript --task <tool_use_id>.

Current repo: gh/petercr/jev-orchestrator  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
  -c, --checkpoint string             Explain a specific checkpoint (ID or prefix)
      --commit string                 Explain a specific commit (SHA or ref, "commit-ish")
      --force                         Regenerate summary even if one already exists (requires --generate)
      --full                          Show full parsed transcript (all prompts/responses)
      --generate                      Generate an AI summary for the checkpoint
      --insecure-http-auth            Allow plain-HTTP auth for --repo (local dev only)
      --json                          Output metadata as JSON (no transcript bytes)
      --limit int                     Cap the list view at N checkpoints (default: 100). Only meaningful with --json.
      --no-pager                      Disable pager output
      --raw-transcript                Show raw transcript file (JSONL format)
      --repo string                   Explain a checkpoint owned by another repo (gh/owner/name, et/project/repo, entire://<host>/gh/<owner>/<repo>, or entire://<host>/et/<project>/<repo>), read from that repo's Entire API
      --search-all                    Search all commits (no branch/depth limit, may be slow)
      --session string                Filter checkpoints by session ID (or prefix)
      --session-index int             Session index within a multi-session checkpoint (0-based, defaults to latest) (default -1)
  -s, --short                         Show summary only (omit prompts and files)
      --summary-timeout-seconds int   Hard deadline in seconds for --generate summary generation; overrides summary_timeout_seconds setting. 0 = use setting; if setting is also unset or 0, no automatic deadline applies.
      --task string                   Subagent task (tool_use_id or agent_id) whose stored transcript --transcript streams
      --transcript                    Stream stored checkpoint transcript bytes to stdout (a session's, or a subagent's with --task)

Inherited flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only — including the git and agent processes it spawns — instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

Implemented the fix locally for [issue #78](https://github.com/petercr/jev-orchestrator/issues/78). Post-worker refresh and approved inspection recovery now retain established validation requirements and add newly detected ones. The CLI names checks that lack runnable coverage, and those checks block both recommended and manual completion.

Regression tests cover both refresh paths and verify that restoring a missing check requires fresh independent validation before completion. `pnpm check`, `pnpm build`, and all 1,649 tests passed.

issues.title: Bind validation coverage to the manifest used for execution
issues.body:
Repository inspection computes which checks a declared package workflow covers. A validation candidate carries the package manager and script name, and execution checks the command shape. Passing evidence is later expanded using the coverage in the repository snapshot. A change to the workflow or a script it references between inspection and execution can leave successful evidence credited against stale coverage. Manifest changes during validation can also make it unclear which definition the result applies to.

- [Validation candidate records the script and command](https://github.com/petercr/jev-orchestrator/blob/1547e2727d3dacc4b6ce885f47c5cb11fa7c21f9/src/orchestration/candidate.ts#L330-L359)
- [Executor checks the package-manager command and invokes it](https://github.com/petercr/jev-orchestrator/blob/1547e2727d3dacc4b6ce885f47c5cb11fa7c21f9/src/orchestration/execute.ts#L204-L252)
- [Validation outcomes expand passing records using snapshot coverage](https://github.com/petercr/jev-orchestrator/blob/1547e2727d3dacc4b6ce885f47c5cb11fa7c21f9/src/repo/validation.ts#L73-L84)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Bind approval and passing coverage to the relevant workflow definitions, including referenced package scripts. A definition change detected before execution requires a fresh candidate and approval.
- [ ] If the definitions cannot be verified across execution, keep affected checks pending and completion blocked. Later inspection must not retroactively expand existing passing evidence.
- [ ] Add deterministic regressions for changes before and during a validation attempt, including a referenced script change. Confirm a stable declared workflow still earns credit for its constituent checks.

issues.title: Apply a consistent secret-path policy to repository reads, searches, and snapshots
issues.body:
## Finding

Repository reads, content searches, and saved-run snapshots use different secret-path exclusions. The snapshot policy already treats `.npmrc` and `.netrc` as sensitive, but the candidate/read policy and search globs omit them. The policies also differ for other credential filenames and key extensions. A sensitive file can therefore be included in repository evidence even when snapshot capture excludes it. [Read candidate policy](https://github.com/petercr/jev-orchestrator/blob/1547e2727d3dacc4b6ce885f47c5cb11fa7c21f9/src/orchestration/candidate.ts#L146-L209) · [Search globs](https://github.com/petercr/jev-orchestrator/blob/1547e2727d3dacc4b6ce885f47c5cb11fa7c21f9/src/orchestration/execute.ts#L91-L130) · [Snapshot exclusions](https://github.com/petercr/jev-orchestrator/blob/1547e2727d3dacc4b6ce885f47c5cb11fa7c21f9/src/saved-runs/snapshot.ts#L26-L30)

## Acceptance criteria

- Define shared secret-path rules and enforce them at candidate selection, read execution, search input and results, and snapshot capture while retaining each operation’s other bounds and exclusions.
- Keep sensitive targets blocked after path resolution. Keep search from inspecting excluded content or returning its paths as evidence.
- Add offline regressions with inert fixture data that cover common credential paths at the root and in subdirectories, case handling, resolved aliases for reads, and normal files that should remain available.
issues.display_title: Apply a consistent secret-path policy to repository reads, searches, and snapshots

issues.title: Preserve required validation commands from long user clarifications
issues.body:
## Finding

The approved clarification path caps the response at 2,000 characters before it records clarification evidence. Validation requirements are extracted later from that stored text. If a supported command falls beyond the display limit, policy can treat the required checks as complete because it receives neither the command nor an omission marker. [Clarification capture](https://github.com/petercr/jev-orchestrator/blob/1547e2727d3dacc4b6ce885f47c5cb11fa7c21f9/src/orchestration/loop.ts#L960-L974) · [Requirement extraction and omission check](https://github.com/petercr/jev-orchestrator/blob/1547e2727d3dacc4b6ce885f47c5cb11fa7c21f9/src/repo/validation.ts#L10-L24)

## Acceptance criteria

- Derive bounded validation requirements from the approved clarification before shortening its display text. Persist the requirements and any omission signal needed by the completion policy across supported continuation paths.
- If an input or requirement limit prevents complete extraction, surface the omission and keep completion blocked pending clarification.
- Add offline regressions for requirements beyond the display limit, overflow handling, and a normal short clarification. Verify that both automatic and manually selected completion still require current-generation independent validation.
issues.display_title: Preserve required validation commands from long user clarifications

issues.title: Discover required root instruction files independently of listing limits
issues.body:
## Finding

Linked-task preparation checks `repo.topLevelFiles` to decide whether `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, or `CLAUDE.md` needs to be read. The general root listing scans up to 256 entries and retains at most 80 sorted names. An existing instruction file can be omitted at either bound, so preparation can leave it unread before validation, delegation, or completion. [Bounded root listing](https://github.com/petercr/jev-orchestrator/blob/1547e2727d3dacc4b6ce885f47c5cb11fa7c21f9/src/repo/inspect.ts#L101-L115) · [Preparation check](https://github.com/petercr/jev-orchestrator/blob/1547e2727d3dacc4b6ce885f47c5cb11fa7c21f9/src/repo/preparation.ts#L4-L34)

## Acceptance criteria

- Discover the fixed root instruction filenames with bounded, read-only probes independent of the displayed root listing. Keep existing read-path safety checks authoritative.
- Use the resulting instruction-file evidence consistently during linked-task candidate selection, manual alternatives, final approval, and supported continuation.
- Add offline coverage for both listing bounds and verify that a known unread instruction still gates validation, delegation, and completion.
issues.display_title: Discover required root instruction files independently of listing limits

issues.title: Scope subprocess environments to validation and worker needs
issues.body:
Approved repository validation scripts and coding workers receive the full parent environment through the shared process runner. This gives repository-owned code access to evaluation-provider credentials and other unrelated ambient credentials. The relevant paths are [the shared spawn boundary](https://github.com/petercr/jev-orchestrator/blob/1547e2727d3dacc4b6ce885f47c5cb11fa7c21f9/src/process.ts#L41-L53) and [validation and worker dispatch](https://github.com/petercr/jev-orchestrator/blob/1547e2727d3dacc4b6ce885f47c5cb11fa7c21f9/src/orchestration/execute.ts#L186-L252).

## Acceptance criteria

- Build a minimal, explicit environment for each subprocess role. Keep evaluation-only credentials and their aliases in the evaluator. Preserve runtime variables needed to find supported tools, and scope any supported worker credentials to the corresponding adapter.
- Construct environments locally at execution and keep values out of candidates, worker prompts, saved runs, and traces. Preserve manual approval, Codex sandbox and networking settings, and process cleanup.
- Add offline tests at the spawn boundary using synthetic values. Verify that validation and each worker receive only their intended environment, including coverage for known provider aliases and an unrelated credential-shaped variable.
issues.display_title: Scope subprocess environments to validation and worker needs

issues.title: Keep trace writes bound to private, verified storage
issues.body:
The trace writer creates the trace directory without checking its identity, allocates an exclusive file, then reopens the pathname for the decision record and for each orchestration append. A redirected or replaced path can send records outside the trace directory or modify another file. Trace records can contain task and repository details even after redaction, and default permissions can expose them on shared machines. See [trace allocation and decision writes](https://github.com/petercr/jev-orchestrator/blob/1547e2727d3dacc4b6ce885f47c5cb11fa7c21f9/src/logging/trace.ts#L216-L250) and [orchestration appends](https://github.com/petercr/jev-orchestrator/blob/1547e2727d3dacc4b6ce885f47c5cb11fa7c21f9/src/logging/trace.ts#L265-L305).

## Acceptance criteria

- Reject unsafe trace directories, including symlinks. Create traces with owner-only access where supported and enforce equivalent privacy on other supported platforms.
- Bind writes to the file created for the run and handle directory and file replacement safely. Retain bounded errors and close resources on normal, interrupted, and failed paths.
- Add offline tests for both trace modes that verify regular JSONL output, restrictive permissions where supported, and that redirected or replaced paths leave unrelated files untouched.
issues.display_title: Keep trace writes bound to private, verified storage

entire search — Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using semantic and keyword matching
Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using hybrid search (semantic + keyword),
powered by the Entire search service.

Requires authentication via 'entire login' (GitHub device flow).

By default, results are scoped to the current repository. Use --all-repos to
search across all accessible repos.

Run without arguments to open an interactive search. Results are
displayed in an interactive table. Use --json for machine-readable output,
and add --compact for a trimmed per-result shape suited to agents (implies
--json): id, type, repo, branch, author, date, files touched, score, match
snippet, and a truncated title instead of the full prompt (repo hits add
description and checkpoint count). Fetch full detail
for a single result with 'entire checkpoint explain <id>', or add --full to
that command to pull the checkpoint's entire session transcript. For a
checkpoint or commit hit from another repo, add --repo gh/<owner>/<repo> for
a GitHub mirror or --repo et/<project>/<repo> for an Entire-native repo. The
forge prefix is required, and the hit's id must be a full checkpoint ID (12-char hex or 26-char ULID) or a full commit SHA
(a SHA is resolved to its checkpoint by that repo's Entire API). Prefixes
cannot be resolved in another repo. This is unrelated to this command's
--repo filter below.

CLI queries also support inline filters like author:<name>, date:<week|month>,
branch:<name>, repo:<owner/name>, and repo:* to search all accessible repos.

Examples:
entire search "retry backoff" --json
  entire search "retry backoff" --json --compact
  entire search "auth timeout author:alice date:week"
  entire search --code "parseToken"

      --compact          Trimmed JSON output for agents: id, repo, files touched, score, match snippet, and a truncated title instead of the full prompt (implies --json)
